setName: Snowflake AI Data Cloud Features & Architecture
domain: Snowflake AI Data Cloud Features & Architecture

questions.question: Snowflake's architecture is described as a hybrid of which two architecture models?

options.text: Shared-disk and shared-nothing
Client-server and peer-to-peer
Monolithic and microservices
Centralized and distributed

questions.explanation: A is correct. Snowflake uses a hybrid architecture combining shared-disk (centralized storage accessible by all compute nodes) and shared-nothing (each compute node processes queries independently using local caching). B, C, and D do not accurately describe Snowflake's architectural model.

questions.question: Which three distinct layers make up Snowflake's architecture?

options.text: Presentation Layer, Application Layer, Data Layer
Database Storage, Query Processing (Virtual Warehouses), Cloud Services
Ingestion Layer, Compute Layer, Output Layer
Client Layer, Middleware Layer, Database Layer

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake's three layers are: Database Storage (stores data in micro-partitions), Query Processing (virtual warehouses that execute queries), and Cloud Services (handles authentication, metadata, optimization, and infrastructure management).

questions.question: Snowflake uses which approach for concurrency handling?

options.text: Pessimistic locking with table-level locks
MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control)
Optimistic locking with row-level locks
No concurrency control; queries are serialized

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake uses MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control), meaning readers never block writers and writers never block readers. Each query sees a consistent snapshot of the data as of the time the query started.

questions.question: In Snowflake, data is stored in which format?

options.text: Row-based format similar to traditional databases
Columnar format in compressed micro-partitions
Key-value pairs in distributed hash tables
Document-based format similar to MongoDB

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake stores data in a proprietary columnar format within compressed micro-partitions. Each micro-partition is 50-500MB of uncompressed data, stored compressed in cloud storage. This columnar approach enables efficient query processing and compression.

questions.question: What is the typical uncompressed size range of a Snowflake micro-partition?

options.text: 1-5 GB

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake micro-partitions contain 50 to 500 MB of uncompressed data. They are organized in a columnar format and automatically compressed, enabling efficient storage and query pruning. The other ranges are incorrect.

questions.question: In Snowflake, what determines how data is organized within micro-partitions?

options.text: Users must manually define partition keys
Data is automatically partitioned based on the insertion order
Data is partitioned based on a hash of the primary key
Data is randomly distributed across partitions

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake automatically organizes data into micro-partitions based on the natural insertion order. Users do not need to define partition keys. While clustering keys can be applied to reorganize data for performance, the default behavior is automatic partitioning by insertion order.

questions.question: What type of storage does Snowflake use for its Database Storage layer?

options.text: Local SSD storage on compute nodes
Cloud object storage (e.g., S3, Azure Blob, GCS)
Network-attached storage (NAS)
On-premises storage arrays

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake stores all table data in cloud object storage provided by the underlying cloud platform (Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, or Google Cloud Storage). Local SSD on compute nodes is used only for caching, not permanent storage.

questions.question: Which statement about Snowflake's storage costs is correct?

options.text: Storage is billed based on the uncompressed size of the data
Storage is billed based on the average compressed size of data stored per month
Storage is free; you only pay for compute
Storage is billed per query based on data scanned

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake storage costs are based on the average amount of compressed data stored each month, including data in tables, Time Travel, and Fail-safe. Because Snowflake compresses data automatically, you pay for the compressed size, not the original uncompressed size.

questions.question: Snowflake stores data in an open file format that can be accessed directly by other tools.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: B is correct (False). Snowflake stores data in a proprietary, optimized columnar format. Data in Snowflake's internal storage cannot be directly accessed by external tools. You must use Snowflake's query engine (SQL) or unload data to access it.

questions.question: What type of storage does Snowflake use to store table data internally?

options.text: Row-based storage in B-tree indexes
Columnar storage in compressed micro-partitions
Document-based storage in JSON format
Key-value store with hash indexes

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake stores data in columnar format within compressed micro-partitions. Each micro-partition contains 50-500 MB of uncompressed data. Columnar storage enables efficient query processing by reading only the columns needed.

questions.question: What is the approximate uncompressed size range of a Snowflake micro-partition?

options.text: 500 MB - 1 GB

questions.explanation: C is correct. Micro-partitions are between 50 and 500 MB of uncompressed data. They are automatically created and managed by Snowflake as data is inserted. Each micro-partition stores metadata about the data it contains for pruning optimization.

questions.question: What metadata does Snowflake automatically store for each micro-partition?

options.text: Only the row count
Range of values for each column, number of distinct values, and NULL counts
Only the file size and creation date
Complete index of all values in every column

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake stores rich metadata for each micro-partition including the range of values (min/max) for each column, the number of distinct values, and NULL counts. This metadata enables efficient partition pruning without requiring manual indexes.

questions.question: Which statement best describes Snowflake's approach to indexing?

options.text: Snowflake requires manual index creation for optimal performance
Snowflake uses automatic micro-partition pruning instead of traditional indexes
Snowflake uses B-tree indexes created during data loading
Snowflake does not support any form of data optimization

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake does not use traditional indexes. Instead, it leverages micro-partition metadata (min/max values per column) to prune partitions that don't contain relevant data. This eliminates the overhead of maintaining indexes.

questions.question: What is Snowflake's approach to data compression?

options.text: Users must manually specify compression algorithms
Snowflake automatically compresses all stored data and chooses optimal compression
Compression is only applied during data loading
Compression is not supported

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake automatically compresses all data stored in micro-partitions. The system chooses the optimal compression algorithm for each column based on the data type and content. Users cannot and do not need to specify compression settings for stored data.

questions.question: How are virtual warehouses billed in Snowflake?

options.text: Per-minute with a minimum of 60 seconds
Per-second with a minimum of 60 seconds
Per-hour with a minimum of 30 minutes
Per-query based on data scanned

questions.explanation: B is correct. Virtual warehouses are billed per-second with a minimum charge of 60 seconds each time they are resumed. This means if a warehouse runs for 65 seconds, you are charged for 65 seconds. If it runs for 30 seconds, you are charged for 60 seconds (the minimum).

questions.question: What is the recommended best practice for AUTO_SUSPEND on a virtual warehouse?

options.text: Set AUTO_SUSPEND = 0 to keep warehouses always running
Set AUTO_SUSPEND between 60 and 600 seconds depending on workload
Never use AUTO_SUSPEND; always manually suspend warehouses
Set AUTO_SUSPEND = 3600 (1 hour) for all warehouses

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake recommends setting AUTO_SUSPEND between 60 seconds and 600 seconds depending on whether you need to keep the warehouse cache warm. Setting it to 0 means the warehouse never auto-suspends, which wastes credits. Manual suspension is impractical for most workloads.

questions.question: Which of the following virtual warehouse sizes has the most compute resources?

options.text: X-Large
2X-Large
4X-Large
6X-Large

questions.explanation: D is correct. Snowflake warehouse sizes range from X-Small to 6X-Large. Each increase in size doubles the compute resources and cost. 6X-Large is the largest available size with the most compute power.

questions.question: When a virtual warehouse size increases by one step (e.g., Small to Medium), what happens to the number of compute resources?

options.text: They increase by 50%
They double
They triple
They increase by a variable amount

questions.explanation: B is correct. Each increase in warehouse size doubles the compute resources (servers/nodes) and correspondingly doubles the credit consumption per hour. For example, X-Small uses 1 credit/hour, Small uses 2, Medium uses 4, and so on.

questions.question: What is the credit consumption per hour for an X-Small virtual warehouse?

options.text: 0.5 credits
1 credit
2 credits
4 credits

questions.explanation: B is correct. An X-Small warehouse consumes 1 credit per hour. Small = 2, Medium = 4, Large = 8, X-Large = 16, 2X-Large = 32, 3X-Large = 64, 4X-Large = 128 credits per hour.

questions.question: Which Snowflake component is responsible for executing SQL queries?

options.text: Cloud Services layer
Database Storage layer
Virtual Warehouses (Query Processing layer)
Result Cache

questions.explanation: C is correct. Virtual warehouses in the Query Processing layer are responsible for executing SQL queries. The Cloud Services layer handles query parsing and optimization but delegates execution to virtual warehouses. The Storage layer stores data but doesn't process queries.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Snowflake virtual warehouses is TRUE?

options.text: Multiple warehouses can share the same compute resources
Each virtual warehouse is an independent compute cluster that does not share resources with other warehouses
Warehouses must be manually provisioned and cannot auto-scale
A single warehouse is shared by all users in an account

questions.explanation: B is correct. Each virtual warehouse is an independent MPP compute cluster with dedicated resources. Warehouses do not compete with each other for compute resources, which is a key advantage of Snowflake's shared-nothing compute architecture.

questions.question: What does the SHOW WAREHOUSES command display?

options.text: Current credit consumption for all warehouses
Properties and status of all warehouses the user has access to
Historical query performance on all warehouses
The internal architecture of each warehouse cluster

questions.explanation: B is correct. SHOW WAREHOUSES displays the properties (name, size, state, auto_suspend, auto_resume, etc.) and status of all warehouses that the current user has privileges to see. It does not show credit consumption details or query history.

questions.question: Can two virtual warehouses access the same data simultaneously without contention?

options.text: No, one warehouse must wait for the other to finish
Yes, because compute and storage are separated
Only if they are in different accounts
Only if the data is replicated to both warehouses

questions.explanation: B is correct. Because Snowflake separates compute from storage, multiple warehouses can access the same data concurrently without any contention or performance impact on each other. Each warehouse has its own independent compute resources.

questions.question: What happens to a virtual warehouse's local disk cache when the warehouse is suspended?

options.text: The cache is preserved indefinitely
The cache is dropped and must be rebuilt when resumed
The cache is saved to cloud storage
The cache is shared with other warehouses

questions.explanation: B is correct. When a warehouse is suspended, its compute resources (including local SSD cache) are released. When resumed, the cache starts empty and must be rebuilt as queries are executed. This is why the first queries after resuming may be slower.

questions.question: What is the default auto-suspend time for a virtual warehouse?

options.text: 5 minutes
10 minutes
15 minutes
Never (warehouses run indefinitely)

questions.explanation: B is correct. The default AUTO_SUSPEND setting is 600 seconds (10 minutes) of inactivity. After this period with no queries, the warehouse automatically suspends to save credits. This can be changed to any value from 0 (immediate) to any number of seconds.

questions.question: Which virtual warehouse size is the smallest available in Snowflake?

options.text: X-Small
Small
Micro
Nano

questions.explanation: A is correct. X-Small is the smallest warehouse size. Warehouse sizes range from X-Small to 6X-Large, with each size doubling the compute resources and credits consumed per hour compared to the previous size.

questions.question: When you double the size of a virtual warehouse (e.g., from Small to Medium), what happens to the credit consumption per hour?

options.text: It stays the same
It doubles
It triples
It increases by 50%

questions.explanation: B is correct. Each warehouse size increase doubles the compute resources and credits consumed. X-Small = 1 credit/hour, Small = 2, Medium = 4, Large = 8, X-Large = 16, and so on.

questions.question: What is the credit consumption per hour for an X-Small warehouse?

options.text: 0.5 credits
1 credit
2 credits
4 credits

questions.explanation: B is correct. An X-Small warehouse consumes 1 credit per hour. Small = 2, Medium = 4, Large = 8, X-Large = 16, 2X-Large = 32, 3X-Large = 64, 4X-Large = 128, 5X-Large = 256, 6X-Large = 512.

questions.question: What does the AUTO_RESUME setting control on a virtual warehouse?

options.text: Whether the warehouse automatically resizes based on load
Whether the warehouse automatically starts when a query is submitted to it
Whether the warehouse automatically refreshes its cache
Whether the warehouse automatically backs up its data

questions.explanation: B is correct. When AUTO_RESUME is enabled (default is TRUE), a suspended warehouse automatically starts up when a query is submitted to it. If disabled, the warehouse must be manually resumed before queries can be executed.

questions.question: What is the minimum billing increment for a virtual warehouse?

options.text: 1 second
60 seconds (1 minute)
10 minutes
1 hour

questions.explanation: B is correct. Virtual warehouses have a minimum billing of 60 seconds (1 minute) when they start up. After that initial minute, billing is per-second. This means even a 5-second query will be billed for at least 60 seconds of warehouse time.

questions.question: What is a Virtual Warehouse in Snowflake?

options.text: A physical data center owned by Snowflake
A named abstraction for a cluster of compute resources used to execute queries and DML
A logical container for storing databases
A network load balancer for distributing queries

questions.explanation: B is correct. A Virtual Warehouse is a named cluster of compute resources (CPU, memory, SSD cache) that Snowflake provisions from the cloud provider. It is used to execute SQL queries, load data, and perform DML operations. It is independent of storage.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Snowflake's Cloud Services layer is TRUE?

options.text: It executes user queries directly
It manages infrastructure, metadata, authentication, and query optimization
It stores data in micro-partitions
It is responsible for data compression and encryption only

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Cloud Services layer handles authentication, access control, infrastructure management, metadata management, query parsing, and optimization. A is wrong â€” query execution happens in the Query Processing layer. C is wrong â€” storage is the Database Storage layer.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Snowflake's metadata store in the Cloud Services layer?

options.text: To store actual table data for fast retrieval
To track micro-partition statistics, file references, and table structure information
To cache query results for all users
To manage virtual warehouse configurations only

questions.explanation: B is correct. The metadata store tracks information about every micro-partition including min/max values, null counts, and the number of distinct values. This metadata enables query pruning, which skips irrelevant micro-partitions during query execution.

questions.question: What happens when Snowflake's Cloud Services layer usage exceeds 10% of the daily warehouse compute usage?

options.text: No additional charges are applied
Only the usage exceeding the 10% threshold is billed
The entire Cloud Services usage is billed
The account is suspended until the next billing cycle

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake provides a daily 10% adjustment where Cloud Services compute is not billed if it stays under 10% of daily warehouse compute. If it exceeds 10%, only the portion above the threshold is charged.

questions.question: Which statement best describes Snowflake's approach to indexes?

options.text: Snowflake requires users to create indexes for optimal query performance
Snowflake does not use traditional indexes; it relies on micro-partition pruning and metadata
Snowflake automatically creates B-tree indexes on primary keys
Snowflake uses bitmap indexes on all columns

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake does not support or require traditional indexes. Instead, it uses micro-partition metadata (min/max values, distinct counts) to prune irrelevant partitions during query execution. This eliminates the overhead of index maintenance.

questions.question: Which Snowflake layer is responsible for authentication, query parsing, optimization, and access control?

options.text: Storage Layer
Compute Layer (Virtual Warehouses)
Cloud Services Layer
Data Layer

questions.explanation: C is correct. The Cloud Services Layer handles authentication, access control, query parsing/optimization, metadata management, infrastructure management, and transaction management. The Compute Layer executes queries, and the Storage Layer stores data.

questions.question: How does Snowflake charge for cloud services layer usage?

options.text: It is always free
A fixed monthly fee
Cloud services are charged only when usage exceeds 10% of daily warehouse consumption
A per-query fee for every query executed

questions.explanation: C is correct. Cloud services compute is included up to 10% of the daily warehouse compute consumption. If cloud services usage exceeds this 10% threshold, the overage is billed separately. Most customers do not exceed this limit.

questions.question: What is Snowsight?

options.text: A command-line tool for managing Snowflake accounts
Snowflake's web-based user interface for querying, visualization, and administration
A data integration tool for ETL pipelines
A third-party monitoring tool for Snowflake

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowsight is Snowflake's modern web-based user interface. It provides SQL editing, query results visualization with charts, dashboards, worksheet sharing, and administrative capabilities â€” all through a browser.

questions.question: What is Snowflake's Snowsight?

options.text: An ETL tool for data loading
Snowflake's web-based user interface for querying, visualization, and administration
A command-line interface for Snowflake
A third-party business intelligence tool

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowsight is Snowflake's modern web-based UI that provides SQL worksheets, data visualization (dashboards and charts), administration features, activity monitoring, and collaboration capabilities.

questions.question: Which Snowflake edition provides the highest level of security including HIPAA and PCI DSS compliance?

options.text: Standard
Enterprise
Business Critical
Virtual Private Snowflake (VPS)

questions.explanation: D is correct. While Business Critical supports HIPAA and PCI DSS compliance, Virtual Private Snowflake (VPS) provides the highest level of security with a completely dedicated and isolated environment. VPS includes all Business Critical features plus dedicated metadata storage and isolated compute.

questions.question: Which Snowflake edition is required for database failover and failback?

options.text: Standard
Enterprise
Business Critical
Any edition

questions.explanation: C is correct. Database failover and failback are available starting with the Business Critical edition. Standard and Enterprise editions support database replication but not failover/failback.

questions.question: Which Snowflake edition is the entry-level offering?

options.text: Enterprise
Business Critical
Standard
Free Tier

questions.explanation: C is correct. Standard is the entry-level edition providing core Snowflake functionality including full SQL support, 1 day of Time Travel, secure data sharing, and all basic features. Enterprise adds features like multi-cluster warehouses, up to 90-day Time Travel, and materialized views.

questions.question: What feature does the Business Critical edition add over Enterprise?

options.text: Multi-cluster warehouses
Enhanced security features including HIPAA/PCI compliance, Tri-Secret Secure, and database failover
Support for semi-structured data
Secure Data Sharing

questions.explanation: B is correct. Business Critical adds enhanced security and compliance features: HIPAA and PCI DSS compliance, Tri-Secret Secure (customer-managed encryption keys), database failover/failback for disaster recovery, and AWS PrivateLink/Azure Private Link support.

questions.question: What is the Virtual Private Snowflake (VPS) edition?

options.text: A self-hosted version of Snowflake
The highest level of security with a completely separate Snowflake deployment and dedicated metadata store
A free version for development purposes
A VPN connection to Snowflake

questions.explanation: B is correct. VPS provides the highest level of security with a completely separate Snowflake environment. It includes all Business Critical features plus a dedicated metadata store and compute pool, fully isolated from other Snowflake customers.

questions.question: What is the Snowflake object hierarchy from top to bottom?

options.text: Organization â†’ Account â†’ Database â†’ Schema â†’ Object
Account â†’ Organization â†’ Database â†’ Schema â†’ Object
Database â†’ Schema â†’ Account â†’ Object
Organization â†’ Database â†’ Account â†’ Schema â†’ Object

questions.explanation: A is correct. The Snowflake hierarchy is: Organization (top level, can contain multiple accounts) â†’ Account â†’ Database â†’ Schema â†’ Objects (tables, views, etc.). This hierarchical structure organizes all Snowflake resources.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between Snowflake accounts and cloud regions?

options.text: A Snowflake account can span multiple cloud regions simultaneously
Each Snowflake account is hosted in a single cloud region on a single cloud provider
All Snowflake accounts share the same global region
Snowflake accounts are region-agnostic and data is distributed globally

questions.explanation: B is correct. Each Snowflake account is provisioned in a specific cloud provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and a specific region within that provider. To have presence in multiple regions, you need multiple accounts with database replication configured between them.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of databases that can be created in a single Snowflake account?

options.text: There is no hard limit; it is effectively unlimited

questions.explanation: C is correct. The default maximum number of databases per Snowflake account is 10,000. This includes permanent, transient, and temporary databases. This limit can be adjusted by contacting Snowflake support.

questions.question: What is a Snowflake Account?

options.text: A user login credential
A self-contained environment with its own URL, users, databases, warehouses, and billing
A database within Snowflake
A virtual warehouse configuration

questions.explanation: B is correct. A Snowflake Account is an independent, self-contained environment with its own URL (account_identifier.snowflakecomputing.com), users, roles, databases, warehouses, and separate billing. Accounts exist within a Snowflake Organization.

questions.question: What is a Snowflake Organization?

options.text: A group of users within a single account
A top-level container that links one or more Snowflake accounts for centralized management
A collection of databases
A billing group for credits

questions.explanation: B is correct. A Snowflake Organization is a top-level construct that groups one or more accounts. It enables centralized account management, cross-account data replication, usage tracking across all accounts, and the ability to create new accounts via the ORGADMIN role.

questions.question: How many databases can a single Snowflake account contain?

options.text: Up to 10
Up to 100
Up to 10,000
There is no hard limit documented; accounts can hold a very large number of databases

questions.explanation: D is correct. Snowflake does not impose a strict hard limit on the number of databases per account. In practice, accounts can contain thousands of databases. Limits are governed by account-level configurations and can be adjusted by Snowflake support if needed.

questions.question: How frequently does Snowflake release new versions of its software?

options.text: Every fortnight
Every week
Every month
Quarterly

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake releases new software versions on a weekly basis. These updates are applied transparently to all accounts without downtime, which is one advantage of the Snowflake SaaS model.

questions.question: Which cloud platforms does Snowflake currently support? (Choose three)

options.text: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
Microsoft Azure
Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
IBM Cloud
Oracle Cloud

questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct. Snowflake runs natively on AWS, Azure, and GCP. It does not run on IBM Cloud or Oracle Cloud. Users can choose their cloud provider and region when creating a Snowflake account.

questions.question: What is Snowflake's approach to managing hardware and software updates?

options.text: Users must schedule maintenance windows for updates
Updates require a brief period of downtime
Snowflake is a SaaS platform; updates are applied transparently with no downtime
Users can choose to delay updates for up to 6 months

questions.explanation: C is correct. As a fully managed SaaS platform, Snowflake handles all hardware and software updates transparently. There is no downtime required, no maintenance windows to schedule, and users benefit from the latest features automatically.

questions.question: In Snowflake, who manages the infrastructure (hardware, patching, upgrades)?

options.text: The customer is responsible for all infrastructure
The cloud provider (AWS/Azure/GCP) manages it
Snowflake manages all infrastructure as a fully managed service
Infrastructure is shared between the customer and Snowflake

questions.explanation: C is correct. Snowflake is a fully managed SaaS platform. Snowflake handles all infrastructure management including hardware provisioning, software installation, patching, upgrades, and tuning. Customers focus only on loading and querying data.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a supported cloud platform for Snowflake?

options.text: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
Microsoft Azure
Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI)

questions.explanation: D is correct. Snowflake runs on AWS, Azure, and GCP. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is not a supported platform for Snowflake deployment.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Snowflake's Information Schema?

options.text: A schema for storing user credentials
A set of system-defined views providing metadata about database objects (tables, views, columns, etc.) within a specific database
A schema for storing audit logs
A backup schema created automatically

questions.explanation: B is correct. Every Snowflake database automatically contains an INFORMATION_SCHEMA with system views like TABLES, COLUMNS, VIEWS, and TABLE_PRIVILEGES. Unlike ACCOUNT_USAGE (which has latency), Information Schema provides real-time metadata but only for the current database.

questions.question: What is the difference between ACCOUNT_USAGE and INFORMATION_SCHEMA?

options.text: They are identical
ACCOUNT_USAGE covers the entire account with up to 365 days of history but has latency; INFORMATION_SCHEMA is real-time but limited to the current database
INFORMATION_SCHEMA is for admins; ACCOUNT_USAGE is for developers
ACCOUNT_USAGE is only available in Enterprise edition

questions.explanation: B is correct. ACCOUNT_USAGE (in the shared SNOWFLAKE database) provides account-wide metadata with up to 365 days of history but has 45 minutes to 3 hours of latency. INFORMATION_SCHEMA provides real-time metadata but is scoped to its containing database and has shorter retention.

questions.question: What is the Snowflake Information Schema?

options.text: A dashboard showing account billing information
A set of system-defined views in each database that provide metadata about objects in that database
A tool for managing user permissions
A staging area for data loading

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Information Schema (INFORMATION_SCHEMA) is a set of system-defined views and table functions available in every database. It provides real-time metadata about database objects, columns, privileges, and usage. Data in Information Schema is typically retained for 14 days.

questions.question: What is the difference between Information Schema and Account Usage?

options.text: They are the same thing
Information Schema has real-time data scoped to a database; Account Usage has up to 365 days of data across the entire account with a latency of up to 45 minutes
Account Usage is real-time; Information Schema has a delay
Information Schema is only available on Enterprise edition

questions.explanation: B is correct. Information Schema provides real-time metadata but only for the current database and retains data for 14 days. Account Usage (in the shared SNOWFLAKE database) covers the entire account, retains data for up to 365 days, but has a latency of 45 minutes to 3 hours.

questions.question: What is the SNOWFLAKE shared database?

options.text: A user-created database that is shared between accounts
A system-provided database containing Account Usage, Organization Usage, and other metadata views
A staging database for data loading
A sample database with demo data

questions.explanation: B is correct. The SNOWFLAKE database is a system-shared database available in every account. It contains schemas like ACCOUNT_USAGE (query history, login history, etc.), ORGANIZATION_USAGE, DATA_SHARING_USAGE, and READER_ACCOUNT_USAGE for monitoring and governance.

questions.question: What is Snowpark?

options.text: A data sharing marketplace
A developer framework that allows writing data pipelines in Python, Java, or Scala with dataframe-style APIs
A monitoring tool for warehouse performance
A backup and recovery service

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowpark is a developer framework that lets you write data transformations and pipelines in Python, Java, or Scala using familiar dataframe-style APIs. Code executes within Snowflake's processing layer, enabling developers to work in their preferred language.

questions.question: How does Snowflake handle data encryption in transit?

options.text: Data is not encrypted in transit
TLS 1.2 or higher is required for all connections
Encryption in transit is optional and must be enabled manually
Only JDBC connections are encrypted

questions.explanation: B is correct. All connections to Snowflake require TLS 1.2 or higher encryption. This is mandatory and cannot be disabled. All data transmitted between clients and Snowflake is encrypted in transit.

questions.question: What is the maximum query timeout limit in Snowflake?

options.text: 1 hour
24 hours
The STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS parameter (default is 48 hours)
No timeout limit exists

questions.explanation: C is correct. The STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS parameter controls the maximum execution time for a query. The default is 172800 seconds (48 hours). It can be set at the account, user, session, or warehouse level.

questions.question: What is Snowgrid?

options.text: A specific virtual warehouse type optimized for grid computing
Snowflake's global cross-cloud and cross-region infrastructure enabling seamless data sharing and replication
A data visualization grid layout in Snowsight
A third-party data integration tool supported by Snowflake

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowgrid is Snowflake's global infrastructure that enables cross-cloud and cross-region data sharing, replication, and collaboration. It allows organizations to share and access data across different cloud providers and regions seamlessly.

questions.question: Which of the following are capabilities enabled by Snowflake's cross-cloud features? (Choose two)

options.text: Replicating databases between accounts on different cloud providers
Running a single query that executes simultaneously on AWS and Azure from one warehouse
Sharing data listings with consumers whose accounts are on a different cloud platform
Automatically migrating all account data to the least expensive cloud provider

questions.explanation: A and C are correct. Snowflake supports cross-cloud database replication between accounts on different providers and allows data listings to be shared with consumers on different cloud platforms via auto-fulfillment. B is wrong â€” a single warehouse runs on one cloud provider. D is wrong â€” Snowflake does not auto-migrate data based on cost.

questions.question: What is cross-cloud auto-fulfillment in the Snowflake Marketplace?

options.text: Automatically selecting the cheapest cloud provider for data storage
Snowflake automatically replicates a provider's listing data to the consumer's cloud platform and region so the consumer can access it locally
Load-balancing marketplace queries across all available cloud regions
Automatically provisioning warehouses for marketplace data consumers

questions.explanation: B is correct. Cross-cloud auto-fulfillment automatically replicates a data provider's listing to the consumer's cloud platform and region, so the consumer can query the data locally without manual data transfer. This is a key Snowgrid capability.

questions.question: What is a region group in Snowflake?

options.text: A physical data center cluster within a single cloud provider
A logical grouping of cloud regions that determines where accounts can replicate data and share listings
A set of warehouses that share compute resources within a region
A billing group that consolidates costs across multiple regions

questions.explanation: B is correct. A region group is a logical grouping of cloud regions. By default, accounts belong to a region group that covers their cloud provider's regions, and replication and data sharing are enabled within a region group. Cross-region-group replication can be enabled by contacting Snowflake support.

questions.question: What is required to make Snowflake data available in multiple cloud regions?

options.text: Store data in a globally distributed object storage bucket
Configure database replication between Snowflake accounts in different regions
Enable multi-region mode on a single virtual warehouse
Enable cross-region caching in the Cloud Services layer

questions.explanation: B is correct. To make data available in multiple regions, you configure database replication between Snowflake accounts in different regions. Each account exists in a single region, so you need separate accounts and replication configured between them.

questions.question: When replicating a database from an AWS account to an Azure account, which statement is TRUE?

options.text: A single Snowflake account can span both AWS and Azure natively
You need a Snowflake account on each cloud provider, and replication is configured between the accounts using the Organization feature
Cross-cloud replication is only available with VPS edition
Cross-cloud replication requires exporting and re-importing data manually

questions.explanation: B is correct. Cross-cloud replication requires separate Snowflake accounts on each cloud provider. Using the Snowflake Organization feature, you link accounts and configure database replication between them. A is wrong â€” a single account cannot span multiple cloud providers. C is wrong â€” replication is available starting from Business Critical edition. D is wrong â€” replication is automatic once configured.

questions.question: In a multi-region Snowflake deployment with database replication, which statement about failover is correct?

options.text: Failover is automatic and requires no configuration
Failover groups must be configured and require Business Critical edition or higher
Failover is only possible within the same cloud provider
Failover is supported on all editions including Standard

questions.explanation: B is correct. Database failover requires Business Critical edition or higher. Failover groups must be explicitly configured to specify which objects (databases, warehouses, etc.) should be replicated and which target account should serve as the failover. C is wrong â€” failover can work across cloud providers. D is wrong â€” Standard and Enterprise do not support failover.

questions.question: What is Snowflake Cortex AI?

options.text: A separate cloud platform for training custom neural networks
A suite of built-in AI and ML functions accessible via SQL that run large language models and ML algorithms within Snowflake
A third-party plugin that connects Snowflake to external AI services
A data visualization library for creating ML model charts

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake Cortex AI provides built-in functions callable via SQL (e.g., SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE) that leverage large language models and ML capabilities. Data stays within Snowflake, eliminating the need for external AI platforms.

questions.question: What does the SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.COMPLETE function do?

options.text: Completes a previously failed SQL query automatically
Generates a text response from a specified large language model given a text prompt
Auto-fills NULL values in a column with predicted data
Finalizes a data loading transaction

questions.explanation: B is correct. SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.COMPLETE takes a model name (e.g., 'mistral-large', 'llama3.1-70b') and a prompt string, then returns a text response generated by the specified LLM. It enables text generation, Q&A, and other generative tasks directly in SQL.

questions.question: What does the SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SUMMARIZE function do?

options.text: Generates aggregate statistics (SUM, AVG, COUNT) for a table
Produces a concise summary of the given input text using a large language model
Creates a visual summary dashboard of query results
Compresses text data to reduce storage consumption

questions.explanation: B is correct. SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SUMMARIZE takes a text input and returns a concise summary generated by a language model. It is useful for summarizing long documents, articles, or text fields stored in Snowflake tables.

questions.question: What does the SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.TRANSLATE function do?

options.text: Converts SQL syntax between different database dialects
Transforms data types between columns in a table
Translates text from one natural language to another
Converts file formats during data loading (e.g., CSV to Parquet)

questions.explanation: C is correct. SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.TRANSLATE translates text between natural languages. It accepts the source text, source language code, and target language code, then returns the translated text. It uses a language model to perform the translation within Snowflake.

questions.question: Which of the following Cortex AI functions perform text analysis rather than text generation? (Choose two)

options.text: SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.EXTRACT_ANSWER â€” extracts an answer from a document given a question
SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.COMPLETE â€” generates text using a large language model
SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SENTIMENT â€” returns a sentiment score for input text
SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SUMMARIZE â€” generates a summary of input text

questions.explanation: A and C are correct. EXTRACT_ANSWER analyzes a document to find a specific answer to a question (analysis/extraction task). SENTIMENT analyzes text and returns a numeric sentiment score from -1 to 1 (analysis task). COMPLETE and SUMMARIZE are generative tasks that produce new text output.

questions.question: What is Cortex Search Service in Snowflake used for?

options.text: Searching for available data listings in the Snowflake Marketplace
Building retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications by creating a hybrid search index over text data in Snowflake
Full-text search across all databases and schemas in an account
Searching query history logs for performance analysis

questions.explanation: B is correct. Cortex Search Service enables building RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) applications by indexing text data for hybrid search that combines vector embeddings and keyword search. It allows LLM-powered applications to retrieve relevant context from Snowflake data before generating responses.

questions.question: Which LLM model families are available through Snowflake Cortex AI's COMPLETE function?

options.text: Only OpenAI GPT models
Only Google Gemini models
Open-source and enterprise models including Mistral, Meta Llama, and Snowflake Arctic
Only proprietary Snowflake-developed models

questions.explanation: C is correct. Snowflake Cortex AI provides access to multiple LLM families including Mistral (e.g., mistral-large), Meta Llama (e.g., llama3.1-70b, llama3.1-8b), and Snowflake's own Arctic models. These run within Snowflake's infrastructure so data does not leave the platform.

questions.question: What type of value does the SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SENTIMENT function return?

options.text: A text label such as 'positive', 'negative', or 'neutral'
A numeric score ranging from -1 (most negative) to 1 (most positive)
A boolean value (TRUE for positive, FALSE for negative)
A JSON object containing detailed emotion analysis

questions.explanation: B is correct. The SENTIMENT function returns a floating-point sentiment score between -1 and 1, where -1 indicates the most negative sentiment and 1 indicates the most positive sentiment. Values near 0 indicate neutral sentiment.

questions.question: What type of data does the Snowflake ML FORECAST function require as input?

options.text: A pre-trained model file uploaded to a Snowflake stage
A time-series dataset with a timestamp column and a target numeric column
An API key for an external forecasting service
A warehouse with GPU compute enabled

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Snowflake ML FORECAST function requires a time-series dataset with at least a timestamp column and a target numeric column to predict future values. The model is trained on historical data using SQL and no external tools or pre-trained models are needed.

questions.question: Which of the following are built-in Snowflake ML model types that can be created and trained using SQL? (Choose two)

options.text: ANOMALY_DETECTION
NEURAL_NETWORK
CLASSIFICATION
DEEP_LEARNING

questions.explanation: A and C are correct. Snowflake provides built-in ML functions including ANOMALY_DETECTION (detects anomalies in time-series data), CLASSIFICATION (predicts categorical labels), and FORECAST (time-series predictions). NEURAL_NETWORK and DEEP_LEARNING are not built-in Snowflake ML model types.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Snowflake's built-in CLASSIFICATION ML function?

options.text: To classify data files by format (CSV, JSON, Parquet)
To train a model that predicts categorical labels for new data based on patterns learned from training data
To categorize database objects by type (table, view, function)
To group virtual warehouses by workload type

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake's built-in CLASSIFICATION function allows you to train a classification model on labeled data using SQL. Once trained, the model can predict categorical labels (e.g., churn/no churn, fraud/not fraud) for new data without requiring external ML tools.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Snowflake's Contribution Explorer?

options.text: To track which users contributed the most queries to the system
To identify which dimensions or segments are the primary contributors to a change in a metric over time
To measure warehouse credit contribution by department
To analyze code contributions in version-controlled stored procedures

questions.explanation: B is correct. Contribution Explorer is a Snowflake ML function that helps users understand which dimensions (e.g., product category, region, customer segment) are the primary drivers behind an observed change in a metric. It automates root-cause analysis for metric changes.

questions.question: What does Cortex Fine-tuning allow users to do?

options.text: Tune virtual warehouse performance parameters for faster queries
Adjust micro-partition sizes for better data compression
Customize a supported large language model using their own data to improve performance on specific tasks
Optimize query execution plans for specific workloads

questions.explanation: C is correct. Cortex Fine-tuning allows users to customize a supported LLM (such as Mistral or Llama) using their own training data stored in Snowflake. This produces a task-specific model with improved performance for the user's domain, and data never leaves Snowflake's security perimeter.

questions.question: What are Snowflake Notebooks?

options.text: A separate application that must be installed locally for Python development
An interactive development environment within Snowsight supporting SQL, Python, and Markdown cells for data analysis and ML workflows
A version control system for Snowflake SQL scripts
A logging tool that records all executed queries for audit

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake Notebooks are an interactive cell-based development environment built into Snowsight. They support SQL cells, Python cells (using Snowpark), and Markdown cells, enabling users to perform data exploration, analysis, ML model development, and documentation in a single interface.

questions.question: What is Snowflake Arctic?

options.text: A cold storage tier for infrequently accessed data
A geographic region group for Nordic cloud deployments
An open large language model family developed by Snowflake, optimized for enterprise AI tasks such as SQL generation and coding
A Snowflake tool for monitoring warehouse compute utilization metrics

questions.explanation: C is correct. Snowflake Arctic is a family of open-source large language models developed by Snowflake. Arctic models are optimized for enterprise workloads such as SQL generation, code generation, and instruction following, and are available through Cortex AI.

questions.question: Which of the following is TRUE about Snowsight Dashboards?

options.text: Dashboards can only be created using third-party BI tools connected to Snowflake
Dashboards are built from tiles that display query results as charts or tables, and can be shared with other users in the account
Dashboards require a dedicated warehouse that cannot be used for other queries
Dashboards are only available in the Enterprise edition or higher

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowsight Dashboards are composed of tiles, each displaying the results of a query as a chart or table. Dashboards can be shared with other users and roles in the account. They are available in all editions and use any warehouse the user has access to.

questions.question: How can Snowsight worksheets be shared with other users?

options.text: Worksheets must be exported as files and shared externally
Worksheets can only be shared via the Snowflake Marketplace
Worksheets can be shared directly with specific users or roles within the same Snowflake account
Worksheets cannot be shared between users

questions.explanation: C is correct. Snowsight worksheets support collaboration by allowing users to share worksheets with specific users or roles within the same account. Shared worksheets can be viewed and, depending on permissions, edited by other users.

questions.question: In Snowsight, how do users switch between roles during a session?

options.text: Users must log out and log back in with a different role selected
Users can switch roles using the role selector in the Snowsight UI without logging out
Roles can only be switched by an ACCOUNTADMIN
A new browser tab is required for each role

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowsight provides a role selector in the user interface that allows users to switch their active role at any time without logging out. The role change takes effect immediately and determines the user's access to objects and actions.

questions.question: What is the purpose of filters in Snowsight Dashboards?

options.text: Filters control which users are allowed to view the dashboard
Filters allow dashboard viewers to dynamically adjust query parameters to interactively explore different data subsets across tiles
Filters determine which virtual warehouse is used for dashboard queries
Filters restrict which roles can modify dashboard tiles

questions.explanation: B is correct. Dashboard filters in Snowsight allow viewers to select values that dynamically adjust the queries behind dashboard tiles. This enables interactive data exploration without editing the underlying SQL, such as filtering by date range, region, or product category.

questions.question: What data profiling information does Snowsight provide when previewing a table?

options.text: Detailed query execution plans for all queries that accessed the table
Complete row-level lineage tracking showing data origins
Column-level statistics such as data distribution, frequent values, and NULL counts displayed visually
Automated data quality scores with correction suggestions

questions.explanation: C is correct. Snowsight's data preview feature includes column profiling that shows data distribution histograms, most frequent values, NULL counts, and basic statistics for each column. This helps users quickly understand their data without writing SQL queries.

questions.question: Which features are available in the Enterprise edition but NOT in the Standard edition? (Choose two)

options.text: Multi-cluster virtual warehouses
Secure data sharing
Up to 90 days of Time Travel
End-to-end encryption (AES-256)

questions.explanation: A and C are correct. Multi-cluster warehouses (auto-scaling clusters) and extended Time Travel (up to 90 days) are Enterprise edition features. B is wrong â€” Secure Data Sharing is available in all editions. D is wrong â€” AES-256 encryption is available in all editions.

questions.question: Which feature is available in the Business Critical edition but NOT in Enterprise?

options.text: Materialized views
Multi-cluster warehouses
Tri-Secret Secure (customer-managed encryption keys)
Search optimization service

questions.explanation: C is correct. Tri-Secret Secure, which combines a Snowflake-maintained key with a customer-managed key for composite encryption, is a Business Critical feature. A and D (materialized views and search optimization) are Enterprise features. B (multi-cluster warehouses) is also an Enterprise feature.

questions.question: What makes Virtual Private Snowflake (VPS) unique compared to Business Critical edition?

options.text: VPS supports more programming languages for stored procedures
VPS provides a completely isolated Snowflake environment with a dedicated metadata store and compute resources not shared with any other Snowflake customers
VPS allows unlimited virtual warehouse sizes beyond 6X-Large
VPS includes built-in ETL tools not available in other editions

questions.explanation: B is correct. VPS provides the highest level of isolation with a completely separate Snowflake deployment, including a dedicated metadata store and compute pool that are not shared with any other Snowflake customers. This goes beyond Business Critical's enhanced security and compliance features.

questions.question: How can a Snowflake account be upgraded from one edition to a higher edition (e.g., Standard to Enterprise)?

options.text: Create a new account on the higher edition and manually migrate all data
Run an ALTER ACCOUNT SET EDITION = 'ENTERPRISE' command
Contact Snowflake support or your account representative to request an edition upgrade, which is applied without data migration
Reinstall Snowflake with the new edition license key

questions.explanation: C is correct. Edition upgrades are handled by Snowflake. You contact Snowflake support or your account representative, and the upgrade is applied to the existing account. No data migration or new account creation is needed â€” all existing data and configurations are preserved.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly maps a Snowflake feature to its minimum required edition?

options.text: Materialized Views â†’ Enterprise
Multi-cluster Warehouses â†’ Standard
Tri-Secret Secure â†’ Enterprise
Database Failover â†’ Standard

questions.explanation: A is correct. Materialized Views require Enterprise edition. B is wrong â€” Multi-cluster Warehouses require Enterprise, not Standard. C is wrong â€” Tri-Secret Secure requires Business Critical, not Enterprise. D is wrong â€” Database Failover requires Business Critical, not Standard.

questions.question: Which of the following are TRUE about zero-copy cloning in Snowflake? (Choose two)

options.text: Cloned objects initially share the underlying micro-partitions with the source object
Cloning creates a complete physical copy of all data immediately
No additional storage is consumed at the time of cloning
Clones cannot be modified independently of the source object

questions.explanation: A and C are correct. Zero-copy cloning creates a metadata-only snapshot that references the same underlying micro-partitions, so no data is physically copied and no additional storage is used at clone time. B is wrong â€” no physical copy is made initially. D is wrong â€” clones are fully independent and can be modified without affecting the source.

questions.question: How does Snowflake's metadata-driven architecture benefit query performance?

options.text: Metadata creates B-tree indexes on frequently queried columns automatically
The Cloud Services layer uses micro-partition metadata (min/max values, row counts, NULL counts) to prune irrelevant partitions before query execution
Metadata precomputes and caches all possible query results
Metadata compresses data at the application level before storage

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake stores rich metadata for each micro-partition including min/max values, distinct value counts, and NULL counts for every column. The query optimizer uses this metadata to prune partitions that cannot contain relevant data, significantly reducing I/O and improving performance.

questions.question: What is a key benefit of Snowflake's separation of storage and compute?

options.text: It eliminates the need for data backups
Storage and compute can be independently scaled and billed, allowing cost optimization for different workloads
It guarantees zero-latency queries at all times
It allows only one user at a time per virtual warehouse

questions.explanation: B is correct. Separating storage and compute means you can scale each independently. You can increase compute (larger or more warehouses) without affecting storage costs, and store more data without needing more compute. Multiple warehouses can also access the same data concurrently.

questions.question: What challenge does 'data gravity' present, and how does Snowflake address it?

options.text: Data gravity is the tendency for large datasets to attract applications and services to where data resides; Snowflake addresses it through cross-region replication and cross-cloud data sharing
Data gravity refers to heavy data compression; Snowflake addresses it by using lightweight columnar formats
Data gravity means data becomes harder to delete over time; Snowflake addresses it with Time Travel retention policies
Data gravity is the increasing cost of storage; Snowflake addresses it by offering unlimited free storage

questions.explanation: A is correct. Data gravity is the concept that large datasets tend to attract applications, services, and additional data to their location, making it hard to move workloads. Snowflake addresses this through Snowgrid capabilities â€” cross-region database replication and cross-cloud data sharing â€” so data can be brought closer to consumers.

questions.question: What does it mean that Snowflake has a cloud-agnostic architecture?

options.text: Snowflake does not use any cloud provider and runs entirely on its own infrastructure
Snowflake provides a consistent experience, feature set, and SQL interface regardless of whether the account runs on AWS, Azure, or GCP
Snowflake automatically moves workloads between cloud providers to optimize cost
A single Snowflake warehouse can span multiple cloud providers simultaneously

questions.explanation: B is correct. Snowflake's cloud-agnostic architecture means the platform provides an identical SQL interface, feature set, and user experience whether the account is deployed on AWS, Azure, or GCP. A is wrong â€” Snowflake runs on top of cloud providers. C is wrong â€” workloads are not auto-migrated between clouds. D is wrong â€” a warehouse runs on a single provider.

questions.question: A virtual warehouse is running and executing two queries. The virtual warehouse is resized to a smaller size. What best describes the resize operation?

options.text: The resize operation succeeds, but the node removal occurs once the active queries are finished.
The resize operation fails as a virtual warehouse cannot be resized while it is running queries.
The queries are stopped, and the virtual warehouse is immediately resized to a smaller size.
The queries are paused while the virtual warehouse is resized to a smaller size.

questions.explanation: You can resize a virtual warehouse anytime, even when they are running queries. When resizing to a smaller size, nodes' removal occurs only when all active queries on those nodes have finished.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is true regarding the Query Processing Layer?

options.text: The query processing layer is responsible for optimizing query plans.
The query processing layer can run multiple compute clusters (virtual warehouses) simultaneously.
The query processing layer is responsible for executing queries.
The query processing layer is responsible for generating query plans.

questions.explanation: The query processing layer is the compute layer through which queries and data processing jobs are executed on the stored data. The compute layer can have multiple clusters for a given Snowflake instance simultaneously. The compute engines in Snowflake are known as virtual warehouses. The cloud services layer performs the query plans and optimization.

questions.question: Snowpark supports which of the following languages?

options.text: Java
Python
Scala

questions.explanation: Java, Scala & Python are all supported by Snowpark. Snowpark is a developer framework that allows writing data transformations and pipelines in these three languages using familiar dataframe-style APIs.

questions.question: Which one of the following objects can NOT be cloned?

options.text: External Stage
Databases
Named Internal Stage
Schemas

questions.explanation: Named Internal Stages cannot be cloned. When a database or schema is cloned, any Snowpipe that points to a Named Internal Stage is not cloned. Named External Stages can be cloned. Since a table stage is associated with a table, it is automatically cloned when the table is cloned. Additionally, external tables cannot be cloned either. Databases, Schema, Tables, etc., can be cloned.

questions.question: Which of the following statements are correct regarding Time Travel & fail-safe storage? Select all that apply.

options.text: There is no fail-safe storage for a transient table.
The maximum allowed Time Travel duration for a transient table is 1 day.
A transient table has 7 days of fail-safe storage.
The maximum allowed Time Travel duration for a transient table is 7 days.

questions.explanation: Transient and temporary tables don't have fail-safe functionality; therefore, data in such tables goes through zero days of fail-safe storage. Also, Transient and Temporary tables have a maximum of 1 day of Time Travel.

questions.question: Which of the following operations can be performed on a cloned table?

options.text: DELETE
CLONE
DROP
SELECT

questions.explanation: All these operations can be performed on a cloned table because a cloned table is just like any other table.

questions.question: Snowflake provides which of the following data protection features automatically? Select all that apply.

options.text: Fail-Safe
Tape Backups
Time Travel
Backups to on-premises
Incremental Backups

questions.explanation: Snowflake provides Time Travel & Fail-Safe. Time Travel enables accessing, retrieving, and recovering past data stored in tables. The time travel can range between one and ninety days. Failsafe storage retains data for an additional seven days after the time travel duration has expired. Failsafe adds another layer of protection against data loss; however, only Snowflake support can recover data from failsafe storage.

questions.question: An administrator cloned a table called Customer to a new table called Prospects. The administrator then proceeds to load new data into the Customer table. What can you expect to happen to the Prospects table? Select all that apply.

options.text: The new data does not show up in the Prospects table.
The new data is loaded successfully into the Customer table only.
The data loading fails as it is impossible to load data into a table that was a source for a cloning operation.
The new data is loaded into the Customer table and its clone, the Prospects table.

questions.explanation: The source and cloned items are independent; thus, modifying data in one will not affect the other. For example, the source table can be dropped altogether, which doesn't affect the cloned table.

questions.question: True/False: Snowflake customers can control the format using which Snowflake stores the data for a table.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Snowflake stores data in a proprietary format on cloud object storage, such as AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, or Google Cloud Storage. Users cannot see the actual files, look at how the data is stored, or access the file directly. Users can not change how Snowflake stores the data behind the scenes.

questions.question: How does a secure UDF differ from a different typical UDF?

options.text: Secure UDF does not use specific SQL optimizations.
Secure UDFs can only be executed by administrators.
Secure UDFs don't allow unauthorized users to see the UDF definition.
Secure UDFs are written in machine language and are compiled into Snowflake's code.

questions.explanation: Specific SQL UDF optimizations may allow data that should be hidden from users to be accessed indirectly via different techniques. Secure UDFs do not use these SQL optimizations, ensuring that users have no access to the underlying data, even indirectly. Furthermore, Secure UDFs allow only authorized users to see the definition and information of secure UDFs (i.e., users who are granted the role that owns the UDF).

questions.question: True/False: Once created, micro-partitions are immutable and cannot be modified.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Snowflake partitions are immutable, which means they cannot be changed once created.

questions.question: True or False: Once the Time Travel retention period has ended for a transient table, historical data for that table can not be recovered by Snowflake support.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Transient and temporary tables don't have fail-safe functionality; therefore, data in such tables goes through zero days of fail-safe storage. Also, Transient and Temporary tables have a maximum of 1 day of Time Travel. Therefore, once the Time Travel period for these tables is complete, there is no way to recover historical data.

questions.question: As part of a data processing pipeline, you are required to store data temporarily in an interim table. The first process in the pipeline deletes all existing data in the interim table and loads new data. Several independent processes in the pipeline use the data in the interim table. You are required to minimize data storage costs. Which type of table will you create?

options.text: External
Temporary
Transient
Permanent

questions.explanation: Based on the requirement, a transient table is a good choice. Transient tables don't have fail-safe storage and have only up to 1 day of Time Travel. A transient table provides a good solution because the data is deleted and reloaded daily in this scenario. Transient tables are also the best option because data must be available across different sessions. Transient tables are available across sessions; independent processes and sessions can access the data in a Transient table.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about micro-partitions is correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Column values can never overlap between micro-partitions.
Snowflake uses a row storage format to store columns in each micro-partition.
Micro-partitions are created and added to a table in the order that new data arrives.
Column values may overlap across micro-partitions.

questions.explanation: Because micro-partitions are immutable and new or changed data must be added to a new micro-partition, similar values may not be in the same physical partition. When micro-partitions are added to a table, they are created in the order that the data came in. When more data is added to a table, another micro-partition or possibly many micro-partitions are created to store the new data. Unlike partitioning in many other databases, in Snowflake, values can overlap between different micro-partitions.

questions.question: Which of the following is an appropriate scenario for creating a Stored Procedure?

options.text: Execute one or more SQL statements that are assembled dynamically.
Convert a character column into a numeric column.
Given two inputs, calculate the MAX of the two values.

questions.explanation: Stored procedures are often used to perform recurring administrative activities, e.g., in a particular organization setting up a new user on the system may require creating the user, granting them several roles, creating a private database from them, etc. These steps can easily be placed in a stored procedure, and then the stored procedure can be called whenever there is a requirement to create a new user.

questions.question: Which of the following criteria must be met for Snowflake to reuse the query result cache for a query? Choose all that apply.

options.text: A new query matches an old query.
The query makes no use of user-defined or external functions.
The query does not make use of runtime functions.
The underlying data that contributes to the query results has remained unchanged.
The table micro-partitions have NOT altered as a result of reclustering or consolidation.

questions.explanation: All of these are correct. Snowflake uses the query result cache if the following conditions are met: A new query matches an old query, and the underlying data contributing to the query results remains unchanged. The table micro-partitions have not changed as a result of clustering or consolidation. The query makes no use of user-defined, external, or runtime functions. Note that queries that use the CURRENT DATE function are eligible for query result caching.

questions.question: A stored procedure can return which type of results?

options.text: Tabular Data
Exe files
Single Value
Binary Executables

questions.explanation: A stored procedure can also return a single value or tabular data if desired; however, it is not a requirement that a stored procedure must return a value.

questions.question: A virtual warehouse was started, used for 45 seconds, and shut down after that. The customer will be charged for how many seconds?

options.text: 315 seconds
3600 seconds
60 seconds
45 seconds

questions.explanation: Snowflake credits are billed on a per-second usage basis. However, note that a minimum of 60 seconds of billing applies, so if a virtual warehouse were started and shut down within the first 1st minute, a minimum of 60-second credit usage would apply.

questions.question: Which Snowflake layer manages the metadata related to micro-partitions, databases, and tables?

options.text: Database Storage
Client Tools
Cloud Services
Query Processing

questions.explanation: The cloud services layer contains and manages a variety of metadata, including details regarding how the data is stored, information on the micro-partitions, metadata regarding the databases and tables in your system, the users, roles and security, and so forth.

questions.question: What of the following Snowflake edition allows data clustering to improve query performance?

options.text: Virtual Private Snowflake
Enterprise
Business Critical
Standard

questions.explanation: All Snowflake editions support data clustering. https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/intro-editions.html

questions.question: True/False: It is possible to disable failsafe entirely for a Snowflake account.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Once the Time Travel period ends, Snowflake keeps the data for a further 7-day period as further protection. This fail-safe can not be disabled or configured. You can NOT change it for a Snowflake account, database, schema, or table. However, you can use Transient or Temporary tables, which have zero days of fail-safe storage. https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-failsafe

questions.question: What is the minimum Snowflake edition that supports a dedicated metadata store?

options.text: Standard
Enterprise
Business Critical
Virtual Private Snowflake

questions.explanation: The VPS edition is meant to provide isolation from other customers; thus, each instance has its own metadata store and compute resources. https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/intro-editions.html

questions.question: Which object types can be recovered using the UNDROP command after they have been dropped? Select all that apply.

options.text: User
Database
Role
Schema
Table

questions.explanation: The UNDROP functionality applies to tables, schemas, and databases. That means you can restore complete databases or schemas and their child objects. https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-time-travel#restoring-objects

questions.question: Failsafe is provided as an alternate means for any Snowflake user to access historical data once the Time Travel retention period has ended.

options.text: False
True

questions.explanation: After the Time Travel period has been completed, the fail-safe storage feature stores data for an additional period of seven days. The fail-safe storage offers additional security against data loss; however, only the Snowflake support team can restore data from the fail-safe storage. Fail-safe is not used by end users to access historical data but to recover from accidental data loss by Snowflake support. https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-failsafe

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Snowflake billing? Select all that apply.

options.text: If a virtual warehouse is suspended, it does not contribute to the cost.
Snowflake billing is based on the actual used storage.
Snowflake billing is based on the number of queries executed.
Snowflake billing is based on the amount of data processed by queries.

questions.explanation: Virtual warehouses in a resumed (active) state contribute to the costs. However, it does not matter if the virtual warehouse is not running a query; if it is resumed, it contributes to the costs. Snowflake charges for data storage in database tables, files staged in internal stages, time travel history, and fail-safe storage. Snowflake doesn't charge on how much data a query processed. https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/cost-understanding-overall#how-are-costs-incurred

questions.question: Which of the following Snowflake editions support database failover and failback between Snowflake accounts, thus providing business continuity and disaster recovery? Select all that apply.

options.text: Business Critical
Standard
Enterprise
Virtual Private Snowflake

questions.explanation: Database failover and failback between Snowflake accounts are provided first in the Business Critical edition and are also available in the virtual private Snowflake (VPS) edition. https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/intro-editions.html
